hook: Google Drops *Gemini 4 Argon*, Its Strongest AI Yet
dek: A new model built for cybersecurity, coding, and long, complex tasks.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Google released *Gemini 4 Argon*, which it calls its most powerful AI model yet, built for coding, research, and writing.

slides.label: Who Gets It
slides.text: Argon is only rolling out to select cyber partners through Google's *Fairwind Program*, its security initiative.

slides.label: Its Specialty
slides.text: Trained for defensive cyber work, Argon can *autonomously find, validate, and patch* critical software vulnerabilities.

slides.label: Other Skills
slides.text: Google says Argon is also strong at debugging, codebase migrations, and parsing long videos and charts.

slides.label: The Claim
slides.text: Google says Argon outscored OpenAI's *GPT-6 Astra* and Anthropic's Fable and Opus on multiple AI benchmarks.

slides.label: The Race
slides.text: OpenAI's Astra, Anthropic's Fable, now Argon, every top lab keeps calling its newest model the *best yet*.

slides.label: Google's Comeback
slides.text: Once seen as behind in AI, Google's Gemini app recently hit *over a billion* monthly users, rivaling ChatGPT.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: As AI tools reshape coding and security work, early access to models like Argon shapes who builds the next wave of tech.

cta_line: The AI race just *leveled up* again
question: Should early access to powerful AI tools like Argon be this limited, or opened up faster?

This drops right after OpenAI's Astra and Anthropic's Fable, each one claiming to be the smartest model out. Google says Argon beats them both on benchmarks, and its Gemini app recently crossed a billion monthly users, putting it right up there with ChatGPT.
